analysis.title: 2026 Deloitte Holiday Travel Survey
key_insights: Holiday travel intent is at a post-pandemic low: 47% of surveyed Americans plan to travel between Thanksgiving and mid-January, down 7 percentage points from 54% in 2025. 27% plan a vacation with paid lodging (down from 32%) and 20% plan only to visit friends or relatives (down from 22%).

Travel incidence among households earning $200K+ fell to 59% from 71% in 2025, the first decline for this group since the post-COVID recovery. Travel intent also fell for the $100K-$199K group (to 48% from 54% overall tier figures shown) and for those under $100K.

Cost is cited by high earners: one in four $200K+ non-travelers cite travel prices as a reason for staying home. The top reason for this group is planning to travel at another time (34% of $200K+ non-travelers, versus 13% under $100K and 24% for $100K-$199K).
Marquee (longest) trip budgets rose 5% overall to $2,792 from $2,662. Budgets rose 11% for travelers under $100K, 3% for $100K-$199K, and fell 4% for $200K+ travelers (to $3,993 from $4,148).

Among travelers, 25% of high-income households report increasing budgets (up from 22%), and 14% of budget increasers say they are not upgrading because travel simply costs more (20% for $200K+). 17% of travelers are downgrading trips, mainly through shorter duration, lower in-destination spend and budget lodging.

Hotel intent rose slightly: 62% of holiday travelers plan hotel stays (59% in 2025). Domestic flight intent was 46% (45% in 2025) and international flight intent 21% (17% in 2025). 50% of travelers plan a flight on their longest trip, up from 47%.

Lodging intent rose across all accommodation types, with cruise intent doubling from a small base. 57% of travelers rank price among their top three lodging selection criteria, more than twice any other attribute.

International share of marquee trips rose to 33% from 29% by the chart's domestic/international split. The source text also says 16% (1 in 7) of marquee trips will be international. Among $200K+ travelers, the share traveling abroad on their longest trip dipped from 37% to 34%, with more heading to Asia (+12 pp) and Africa/Middle East.

Premium cabin mix is shifting: international flyers booking first or business class fell to 16% from 20%, while upgraded economy rose to 35% from 31%. 45% of surveyed flyers buy upgraded tickets. Top-tier airline loyalty members are 3x as likely to buy business class (31% vs. 10%).
Millennial travel intent fell 12 pp to 53% from 65%, the largest drop of any generation, and paid-lodging intent fell 10 pp to 31%. 48% of millennials have children under 18 at home.

Gen Z budgets rose 13% on improved financial sentiment: 56% of Gen Z say their finances improved versus 42% in 2025. Boomer budgets rose 7% and Gen X 5%, while millennial budgets fell 3% (as read from the chart's generation labels).

Financial sentiment among $200K+ households deteriorated, while lower-income brackets improved somewhat. Overall, 35% feel better off (33% in 2025), 34% the same and 31% worse. 82% of Americans say everyday expenses affect their ability to spend on travel, most calling it moderate.

Booking channels that allow price comparison gained share. Direct brand booking fell to 75% from 78% for flights and to 69% from 75% for hotels. Online travel agency use for flights was 13% (10% in 2025) and for hotels 14% (11% in 2025).

Gen AI use in travel planning reached 29% of respondents in 2026, versus 24% in 2025, 16% in 2024 and 8% in 2023. Adoption growth is slowing. Millennials use it most. 61% of gen AI users use it for activities and attractions, and 56% for dining.

Thanksgiving remains the busiest period: 31% of trips begin Thanksgiving through end of November, 28% Christmas through New Year's Eve, 24% in December before Christmas, 11% in January. 27% of Americans plan to travel over Thanksgiving. January trips are the longest and most likely to be international or on a cruise.

Luxury travelers are 9% of surveyed holiday travelers and are not defined by income. They participate in in-destination activities at 1.5x to 1.6x the rate of others. Family travelers skew higher income, and the share of family travelers planning a cruise nearly doubled.

Airline loyalty: about 65% of mid-tier and above members say flight redemption benefits meet expectations, while about one in four say they fall short. Onboard experience, airport experience and disruption handling have the largest shortfalls for high-status members. For hotel loyalty, issue resolution and redeeming for non-hotel rewards have the lowest satisfaction.

sector_views.rationale: Overall holiday travel incidence is down, led by high earners, but those who travel are expanding budgets, shifting toward hotels, cruises and upgraded economy, and time-bound demand keeps travel a priority.

macro_indicators.indicator: Holiday travel intent (share of Americans planning to travel Thanksgiving to mid-January)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Lowest in four years in this survey series. Cost pressure on high earners is a negative read for discretionary travel demand, though the figure is a stated intent from a survey and not a spending print.
macro_indicators.period: 2026 holiday season (survey fielded Sept. 28 to Oct. 2, 2026)

macro_indicators.indicator: Household financial sentiment (share saying finances are better than a year ago)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Sentiment worsened for $200K+ households and improved for lower-income brackets.

risk_factors: Cost concerns reaching $200K+ households, the group that had held travel intent steady for three years.
Higher airfare and hotel rates cited as reasons for not traveling.
Everyday expenses affecting travel spending for 82% of Americans.
Millennial parents facing cost pressure, with the largest drop in travel and paid lodging intent.
Survey margin of error is ±2 percentage points for the full sample, and subgroups such as $200K+ travelers (n=268 for some cuts) are smaller.
charts_described: Holiday travel intent 2023 to 2026: total traveling 48%, 49%, 54%, 47%; vacation with paid lodging 29%, 30%, 32%, 27%; visiting friends or relatives only 19%, 19%, 22%, 20%.
Longest trip budgets by generation, 2025 vs 2026, with changes of +7%, +13%, +5% and -3%.

key_data_points.anchor: An independent online research panel was used to survey 4,272 Americans

tension_points.bull_case: Nearly half of surveyed Americans still plan to travel. Travelers are expanding budgets (+5% on the marquee trip), hotel and cruise intent is up slightly, 34% of $200K+ non-travelers plan to travel later, and high-income travelers' trips are longer (39% plan a week or more, up from 36%).
tension_points.bear_case: Travel intent is at a post-pandemic low, with $200K+ incidence down to 59% from 71%, $200K+ budgets down 4%, and fewer high earners booking first or business class. One in four high-earner non-travelers cite travel prices.

theme_stances.key_argument: Cost concerns have reached the highest income level, leading a pullback in holiday travel across income groups.
theme_stances.evidence: Fewer Americans at that highest income level plan to travel than in any holiday season since 2022

theme_stances.key_argument: Travelers still going are expanding budgets, shifting to upgraded economy and hotels, and choosing destinations where dollars go further.
theme_stances.evidence: The upcoming holiday travel rush may be a little quieter overall
